task.description: HARD GATE. Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req027-definition-core-schema.md (commit a15bce4, 1295 lines) against REQ-027's five acceptance criteria and WF-02 Step 1b's checklist (a)-(e). Read the artefact and its cited sources directly -- never CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary as a substitute. Four things need genuine re-derivation rather than inheritance, listed in the dispatch prompt: the R-Co live-schema CASCADE contradiction, the Ecto.Enum case-dump consequence for the partial unique index, the vendored-Ecto partial-index API, and the manifest preserving all seven existing entries while adding two.
acceptance_criteria: priv/repo/migrations gains process_definitions and instance_definition_snapshots migrations, both schema-per-tenant via REQ-022's :prefix mechanism, applying cleanly
process_definitions has a unique index on (name, version) and a partial unique index on name WHERE status = 'active'
process_definitions has a nullable stage column and a partial index on stage WHERE stage IS NOT NULL, per definition.md's PD-07 section (migrations/014_definition_stage.sql)
instance_definition_snapshots.definition_id references process_definitions.id with no ON DELETE CASCADE, and the moduledoc states this is deliberate per PD-08
both Ecto.Schema modules' @moduledoc cite R-Co src/design/definition.md (PD-01/PD-07/PD-08 sections) as the ported source

result.summary: Independently read lib/letflow/design/req027-definition-core-schema.md in full (all 1295 lines, commit a15bce4) and re-derived every verdict from the primary sources it cites; CODE-DESIGNER's step-01 result.summary was not used as evidence for anything. REQ-027's 5 acceptance criteria were grepped out of docs/requirements.yaml:1187-1192 and match this handoff's task.acceptance_criteria byte-for-byte; REQ-027's full description (docs/requirements.yaml:1147-1186) was read clause by clause against the design's own clause-by-clause map at lines 1275-1295. VERDICT PASS on all five WF-02 Step 1b checks, for all five acceptance criteria. === CHECKLIST (a)-(e). === (a) Concrete design element, no deferrals, for every AC: AC1 -> section 4's two named migration files with module names and the #8-before-#9 FK ordering constraint, section 2.1's mandatory if prefix() guard shape, section 2.2 + 5.3's manifest registration, section 4.1's three filename/version constraints, section 4.2's exact :prefix placement, section 4.3's reversibility statement (no execute/1, no raw SQL), and section 4.5's information_schema demonstration method including the negative check against public; AC2 -> section 3.1.2's index table rows uq_definition_version and uq_active_definition with the exact create unique_index calls, plus INV-DEF-1/2/3; AC3 -> section 3.1's stage row (nullable, no default) and section 3.1.2's idx_def_stage row with the exact create index call, plus INV-DEF-4; AC4 -> section 3.2.2's full references/2 shape with per-element mechanism, section 3.2.3's why-:nothing-not-:restrict, section 7.2's verbatim moduledoc, INV-DEF-5; AC5 -> sections 7.1 and 7.2's verbatim moduledoc blocks. grep -niE 'TBD|TODO|FIXME|to be implemented|to be determined|to be decided|will be decided|left open|figure out|unclear|not sure|placeholder for' over the artefact returns ZERO hits. (b) Signatures fully specified: section 5.2 gives @type t and @type status plus full @spec for ProcessDefinition.create_changeset/2 and update_changeset/2 and InstanceDefinitionSnapshot.create_changeset/2, each with its cast list, validate_required list, validate_length bounds and named unique_constraint/foreign_key_constraint targets; section 5.3 states tenant_scoped_migrations/0's @spec is unchanged. A normative 'functions that will deliberately NOT exist' table (6 rows) bounds the surface. (c) Error shape stated, not implicit: section 5.2's opening paragraph explicitly states these are changeset builders returning Ecto.Changeset.t(), that the {:ok, struct} | {:error, changeset} boundary is Repo.insert/2's inside REQ-030/REQ-033, and -- load-bearing -- that a DB violation surfaces as {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} ONLY because the named unique_constraint/foreign_key_constraint declarations are present, otherwise Ecto.ConstraintError is raised. That is an explicit reasoned position satisfying docs/guides/backend_developer_guide.md section 3.5 (read directly, lines 120-127: 'Every @spec states the error shape -- don't leave it implicit'), not an omission. (d) Cross-module dependencies: section 8's table names 13 dependencies with direction and nature, including the REQ-030 contract points (a)-(f) and REQ-033 contract points (a)-(d). (e) No implementation code: grep -nE '^\s*(defmodule|def |defp |use |import |alias |require )' over the artefact returns exactly one hit, line 1178, which is the English word 'use' opening a prose sentence ('use a to_tsvector GIN index at all'). All 18 code fences contain only field(...)/timestamps(...) declarations, @spec/@type lines with comment-annotated cast lists, pseudo-shape blocks (colon-terminated 'if/else/do nothing' lines that are not valid Elixir), moduledoc prose, or SQL SELECTs for the demonstration method -- the identical standard this gate applied to req023-event-store-schema.md, whose section 5.1 uses the same field(...) declaration form (req023 design lines 723-733). === RE-DERIVATION 1: the R-Co live-schema CASCADE contradiction. CONFIRMED, and declining to port it is the RIGHT CALL. === Opened C:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co\migrations\1106_iss0125_instance_definition_snapshots_cascade.sql in full (91 lines). Lines 78-88 do exactly what the design claims: EXECUTE format ALTER TABLE instance_definition_snapshots DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey, then ADD CONSTRAINT of the same name FOREIGN KEY (definition_id) REFERENCES process_definitions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE. So R-Co's live per-tenant schema DOES cascade today. Opened R-Co/src/design/definition.md:2029-2059 ('Atomicity guarantee'): lines 2051-2053 state the column 'references process_definitions(id) but carries no ON DELETE CASCADE'; 2055-2057 state 'Deletion of the source definition does NOT automatically remove snapshot rows. Snapshot rows persist with their captured graph, definition_name, and definition_ver regardless of what happens to the source definition'; 2058-2059 give the hard-deleted-DRAFT edge case. The PD-08 traceability table (line ~2190) repeats 'FK on definition_id has no ON DELETE CASCADE; snapshot row persists independently of source definition lifecycle'. Opened R-Co/migrations/004_definitions.sql in full (69 lines): line 61 is definition_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES process_definitions(id) with no ON DELETE clause, matching the prose. The contradiction the design reports at section 10 C-1 is therefore real and correctly characterised, and section 7.2's moduledoc quotes PD-08's two sentences verbatim and correctly. MY INDEPENDENT JUDGEMENT, weighing 1106's own stated reason as instructed: 1106's header (lines 4-12) gives the root cause as a TEST-HARNESS problem -- 'bespoke per-test cleanup helpers that swallowed SQL errors could silently proceed to DELETE FROM process_definitions after a failed child delete, producing C23503' -- and the same header concedes the shared harness (tests/integration/helpers.zig resetTestData) 'was correctly ordered'. R-Co therefore widened a PRODUCTION referential action to accommodate defective TEST cleanup code. That is the same shape core-directives.md forbids under 'Never satisfy a gate by editing what it measures': the NO ACTION FK was the detector reporting an ordering bug (C23503), and 1106 silenced the detector rather than fixing the helpers. Its rationalisation at lines 14-18 ('the parent row's identity has no meaning without its children once the parent is gone') also inverts PD-08's entire premise, which is that the snapshot is meaningful precisely WITHOUT its parent. So the design's decision is right on Letflow's own governance (REQ-027 AC 4 at requirements.yaml:1191 mandates no cascade and REQ-033 AC 4 at requirements.yaml:1492 mandates the surviving-snapshot behaviour, neither of which a validator may override), and independently right on the merits of 1106's own reasoning. I judge the design slightly UNDERSELLS its position by framing C-1 as 'not a judgement call' -- it is a judgement call, and it wins on the merits too. DISCLOSURE ADEQUACY: adequate, and better than the minimum. The critical property is placement -- section 7.2's verbatim moduledoc paragraph lives in the .ex source a cross-checking agent will actually be editing, names the exact file (migrations/1106_iss0125_instance_definition_snapshots_cascade.sql), gives its stated test-harness motive, says it 'directly contradicts the PD-08 design text quoted above', and states the concrete harm plus a checkable downstream consequence ('would destroy exactly the data this table exists to preserve, and would break REQ-033's fourth acceptance criterion'). Backed by INV-DEF-5, section 10 C-1 and the section 11 AC4 traceability row. One residual gap recorded as MINOR below: the disclosure is prose only, and the mechanical backstop it leans on (REQ-033 AC 4) is itself defective per the design's own OQ-2 / ISS-0024. === RE-DERIVATION 2: the status-case decision. CONFIRMED CORRECT, AND FORCED. === Opened deps/ecto/lib/ecto/enum.ex directly. Lines 81-83: the cond's first clause is `is_list(values) and Enum.all?(values, &is_atom/1) -> validate_unique!(values); {:string, Enum.map(values, fn atom -> {atom, to_string(atom)} end)}`, and line 106 builds on_dump from those mappings. So a bare atom list dumps :active as the lowercase string 'active' -- exactly as claimed. Lines 85-88 are the keyword-list form that maps each atom to an explicit stored value. Opened deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/postgres/connection.ex:1314-1348: line 1344 is if_do(index.where, [' WHERE ', to_string(index.where)]), so the predicate string reaches Postgres verbatim; deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/migration.ex:943-945 documents the same ('its value is passed to the generated WHERE clause as-is'). Therefore if the design had reused REQ-023's keyword form values: [active: 'ACTIVE', ...] while keeping AC 2's mandated predicate WHERE status = 'active', uq_active_definition would index zero rows and PD-03's single-active-per-name invariant would be silently unenforced -- no error, no failing query. The failure mode the design describes is real and exactly as stated. The resolution is not merely correct, it is FORCED: AC 2 (requirements.yaml:1189) fixes the predicate literal as lowercase 'active' and REQ-027's description (requirements.yaml:1156-1158) names the lowercase atoms, so the dump must be lowercase; there is no other internally consistent choice available. I also verified the sibling is self-consistent rather than contradictory: lib/letflow/event_store/instance_projection.ex:48-49 uses values: [active: 'ACTIVE', ...] AND priv/repo/migrations/20260816120003_create_instance_projections.exs uses default: 'ACTIVE' with where: "status = 'ACTIVE'" -- uppercase on both sides. Each design is internally consistent in its own case; that self-consistency, not the case itself, is the property that matters. INVARIANT RECORDING: adequate. Recorded in three places, the load-bearing one being section 7.1's verbatim moduledoc paragraph, which states the dump/predicate coupling, the silent-failure consequence and 'Changing either one without the other is a defect' -- in ProcessDefinition's own source, which is where REQ-030's implementer (whose activate/1 depends on this index, requirements.yaml:1325-1335) will be reading. Also INV-DEF-3 (section 6) and section 10 C-3. Same prose-not-gate residual as re-derivation 1, folded into the MINOR below. === RE-DERIVATION 3: the vendored-Ecto partial-index API. ALL CLAIMS CONFIRMED against the actually vendored deps. === mix.lock:5-6 and :14 confirm ecto 3.14.1, ecto_sql 3.14.0, postgrex 0.22.4, so the deps/ tree read is the one that will build. (i) deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/migration.ex:1050-1051: `def unique_index(table, columns, opts) when is_list(opts), do: index(table, columns, [unique: true] ++ opts)` -- literally index/3 with [unique: true] prepended, so :where/:name/:prefix are all available on a partial UNIQUE index. Confirmed. :where is documented as an index/3 option at migration.ex:884-885 and validate_index_opts!/1 at :1739-1743 permits at most one :where ('To specify multiple conditions, write a single WHERE clause using AND between them'). (ii) Predicate emitted verbatim: connection.ex:1344 as above. Confirmed. (iii) on_delete: :nothing emits NO ON DELETE clause: connection.ex:1906-1918 has explicit clauses for :nilify_all, {:nilify,_}, :default_all, {:default,_}, :delete_all (' ON DELETE CASCADE', line 1916) and :restrict (' ON DELETE RESTRICT', line 1917), then the catch-all `defp reference_on_delete(_), do: []` at line 1918. So :nothing falls through to [] and Postgres applies its default NO ACTION. Confirmed -- this is AC 4's exact mechanism. (iv) type: :binary_id mandatory: migration.ex:509-519's %Reference{} defstruct has column: :id (512), type: :bigserial (513), on_delete: :nothing (514). Confirmed. Supporting claims also verified: index prefix is per-index not inherited (connection.ex:1335 renders quote_name(index.prefix, index.table) from the %Index{}'s own field); a %Reference{} with no :prefix in options falls back to the referencing table's prefix (connection.ex:1872, quote_name(Keyword.get(ref.options, :prefix, table.prefix), ref.table)), so the FK stays inside the tenant schema; the default constraint name is quote_name("#{table.name}_#{column}_fkey") (connection.ex:1895-1896) = instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey, byte-identical to the name R-Co uses at 1106:80 and :85. Type mapping verified at connection.ex:2058-2075 (:binary_id->uuid at 2063, :string->varchar at 2064, :map->postgres_map_type at 2067 whose default is 'jsonb' per deps/ecto_sql/mix.exs:48, :utc_datetime_usec->timestamp at 2071, ecto_to_db(atom)->Atom.to_string at 2075 so :text passes through), varchar sizing at connection.ex:1857 (type == :string -> [type_name, '(255)']), map column defaults at connection.ex:1708-1712 (JSON-encoded and single-quoted, so default: %{'nodes' => [], 'edges' => []} is legal without fragment/1), fragment defaults at connection.ex:1714-1715, and timestamps/1 at migration.ex:1366-1376 (merges Runner.repo_config(:migration_timestamps, []) at 1367 -- grep over config/ for migration_timestamps returns NO matches, confirming section 3.1.1's claim -- defaults type :naive_datetime at 1370, supports the :inserted_at rename at 1371/1374, and adds no DB-level default). No API mistake found; none of the three index-shaped acceptance criteria will fail at implementation time on an Ecto-API ground. === RE-DERIVATION 4: the manifest. CONFIRMED CORRECT. === Opened lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:183-276. @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest at :192-207 currently holds exactly SEVEN entries, every one in the three-element {version, module, filename} form: REQ-023's six (20_260_816_120_001 CreateEvents through 20_260_816_120_006 CreateEventIdempotency) plus REQ-024's 20_260_816_163_103 CreateEventTypeRegistry. Design section 5.3 appends entries eight and nine in that same three-element form, preserving all seven, and explicitly forbids the bare {version, module} form with the correct reason (Ecto.Migrator's load_migration!/1 requires Code.ensure_loaded?, and priv/repo/migrations/*.exs is never compiled -- verified myself at mix.exs:20-21, `defp elixirc_paths(:test), do: ["lib", "test/support"]` / `defp elixirc_paths(_), do: ["lib"]`). tenant_scoped_migrations/0's @spec at :255 is [{version :: pos_integer(), module()}] and the design leaves it unchanged -- correct, since the third element is consumed by the private ensure_migration_module_loaded!/2 (:266-276) and dropped by the Enum.map at :257-260. The design also correctly requires the stale 'seven entries in total' strings at the manifest header comment (:188-191) and the @doc (:216-217) be updated to nine, which is drift this requirement itself introduces. === THE TWO SHIPPED POLICING TESTS -- rule verified, not trusted. === Read test/letflow/event_store/migrations_test.exs:441-561. The section-4 guard test (describe at :441) iterates TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations(), asserts the list is non-empty (:483, guarding against vacuity), runs each entry through Ecto.Migrator.run(Letflow.Repo, [{probe_version, module}], :up, all: true, log: false) with NO :prefix under a synthetic probe version, and asserts public_tables() == tables_before at :499. It needs no edit to cover REQ-027's two migrations the moment section 5.3's entries land -- the design's section 4.4 claim is accurate. The manifest consistency test (describe at :516) computes, at lines 541-542, expected_basename = "#{version}_#{Macro.underscore(List.last(Module.split(module)))}.exs", asserts the module's module_info(:compile)[:source] basename equals it (:544) and that the file exists in priv/repo/migrations (:547); a second test (:552) asserts versions are unique and strictly ascending. I applied that exact rule rather than trusting the design's paraphrase: Macro.underscore('CreateProcessDefinitions') = 'create_process_definitions' and Macro.underscore('CreateInstanceDefinitionSnapshots') = 'create_instance_definition_snapshots', so the design's proposed 20260816193001_create_process_definitions.exs and 20260816193002_create_instance_definition_snapshots.exs satisfy it exactly. Ordering constraint (a) also verified: ls priv/repo/migrations shows 14 files with maximum version 20260816163103, and both proposed versions sort strictly after it and preserve #8-before-#9. Both shipped tests will pass against this design as specified. === REQ-022 SECTION 4, BOTH HALVES. === Read lib/letflow/design/req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md:340-395 directly. Lines 369-387 mandate the guard (branch on Ecto.Migration.prefix()'s truthiness, no-op on the nil branch); lines 389-395 state verbatim that both halves are mandatory -- guard without registration is 'inert forever', registration without the guard 'actively corrupts public on every plain mix ecto.migrate run'. The design supplies BOTH: section 2.1 gives the guard shape (with the else branch doing nothing at all) and section 2.2 plus section 5.3 give the registration. The shipped reference the design cites was confirmed: priv/repo/migrations/20260816120003_create_instance_projections.exs wraps its entire change/0 body in `if prefix() do ... end` with no else branch, uses create table(:instance_projections, primary_key: false, prefix: prefix()), and carries the partial-index precedent create index(:instance_projections, [:status], name: :idx_proj_status, where: "status = 'ACTIVE'", prefix: prefix()) -- the exact shape section 3.1.2 proposes for idx_def_stage. The references/2 precedent at 20260816120004_create_event_payload_store.exs was likewise confirmed to pass column:, type: :binary_id and on_delete: explicitly. === AC 4 AND AC 5 MODULEDOC TEXT. === Sections 7.1 and 7.2 give full verbatim paragraph blocks, not paraphrase instructions, so a later checker can match them literally. AC 4's demand ('the moduledoc states this is deliberate per PD-08') is discharged by section 7.2 paragraph 2, which names PD-08's 'FK without ON DELETE CASCADE' paragraph and quotes definition.md:2055-2057 verbatim -- I diffed the quote against the source and it is accurate word for word. AC 5's demand is discharged by section 7.1 opening 'Ported from R-Co's src/design/definition.md -- the PD-01 sections ... and the PD-07 section ...' and section 7.2 opening 'Ported from R-Co's src/design/definition.md PD-08 section ...' with a PD-01/PD-07 cross-reference. Section 7.3 adds four further required moduledoc claims. Concrete enough to be checked literally: YES. === OPEN QUESTIONS: ALL EIGHT GENUINELY OPEN, NONE BLOCKS AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION. === OQ-1 (tenant_id supplier): premise verified by reading REQ-030's full description at requirements.yaml:1287-1346 -- it never mentions tenant_id, and R-Co's CreateParams has no such field, while R-Co sidesteps it via DEFAULT bpm_effective_tenant_id() (028_adp02) which Letflow has no equivalent of. Genuinely open; this is ORCH's already-filed ISS-0025 (#83) and is NOT re-filed here. Does not block AC 1 (a NOT NULL column with no default applies cleanly to an empty table) or any other AC. OQ-2 (REQ-033 AC 4 undemonstrable under NO ACTION): premise verified against requirements.yaml:1492's literal wording 'where FK rules permit, e.g. a DRAFT definition'; correct that no delete of a referenced definition ever succeeds under NO ACTION. Already ORCH's ISS-0024 (#82), NOT re-filed. Does not block REQ-027 AC 4, which only requires the FK exist without CASCADE and the moduledoc say so. OQ-3 (graph map<->struct conversion): premise verified at lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex:121-136 -- defstruct nodes: [], edges: [] with @spec validate_graph(t()) :: result(), i.e. struct-typed, while this column stores a string-keyed map. Genuinely open and correctly deferred to REQ-030/029; the design still DECIDES the field type (:map) rather than deferring it, so nothing is left unspecified here. OQ-4 (after_created cursor ties): a REQ-030 API decision; the design still picks :utc_datetime_usec rather than deferring. OQ-5 (''-vs-NULL stage, InitialStatusNotDraft): premise verified in R-Co src/definition/store.zig:289 (VALUES ... NULLIF($3, ''), 'DRAFT', ..., NULLIF($6, '')) and requirements.yaml:1304-1305 ('hard-codes status: draft (caller cannot override, no status field on the create params)'). Write-path semantics for REQ-030, not schema shape; AC 3 is fully specified regardless. OQ-6 (no owner for a hard-delete path): premise verified -- REQ-030's function list at requirements.yaml:1300-1341 is create/get_by_id/get_active_by_name/list/activate/deprecate/archive with no delete/1. Genuinely open. OQ-7 (timestamptz project-wide): inherited from req023's OQ-5, still open; grep over config/ for migration_timestamps confirms nothing settles it. OQ-8 (GIN index deferred): premise verified at definition.md:3008-3022 ('A new SQL migration is NOT needed for PD-10 ... Correctness does not require a GIN index ... can be introduced as a standalone migration in a future sprint') and definition.md:2862-2864 (WHERE name ILIKE $2 OR description ILIKE $2). Informational. NONE of the eight blocks any of REQ-027's five acceptance criteria. === CONTRADICTIONS C-1..C-7 SPOT-CHECKED. === C-1 confirmed above. C-2 confirmed (004:42-44 creates idx_def_fts USING GIN(to_tsvector(...)) while definition.md:3008-3022 says no migration is needed and PD-10's actual query is ILIKE, which cannot use a tsvector GIN index -- the design's technical judgement is sound). C-3 confirmed above. C-4 confirmed against requirements.yaml:1336-1340, which already lists exactly the three corrected edges, so the design's 'no action needed' is right. C-5 confirmed (definition.md:376-381 names ON CONFLICT (name, version) while store.zig:290 is a bare ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING with the schema-variant rationale at :282-286). C-6 confirmed and correctly classified as NOT a contradiction (store.zig:289's NULLIF resolves it). C-7 confirmed on both legs: definition.md:362 does claim 'FK to process_instances.id', 004:60 declares instance_id UUID PRIMARY KEY with no REFERENCES clause, and `grep -rn process_instances migrations/` across R-Co returns ZERO hits -- no such table exists. === CITATION SPOT-CHECK. === Roughly 40 of the design's file:line citations were opened and confirmed across requirements.yaml, req022's and req023's designs, tenant_provisioning.ex, mix.exs, mix.lock, config/, four ecto/ecto_sql source files, the shipped instance_projections and event_payload_store migrations, instance_projection.ex, graph.ex, migrations_test.exs, and R-Co's 004/014/028/1106 SQL, definition.md, store.zig and adp-02. Every substantive mechanism was real and correctly characterised; NO fabricated citation was found. Six immaterial line-number drifts are aggregated as a single MINOR below. Four MINOR, non-blocking observations are recorded in result.issues; none is a Step 1b check failure, and ISS-0024/ISS-0025 are deliberately not re-filed.

issues.description: The no-CASCADE invariant (INV-DEF-5) and the status-case invariant (INV-DEF-3) are disclosed in PROSE only -- design sections 7.1/7.2 moduledoc text plus section 6. Nothing mechanically fails if a later agent changes on_delete: :nothing to :delete_all, or changes the Ecto.Enum form without changing the uq_active_definition predicate. The design's section 7.2 leans on REQ-033's fourth acceptance criterion as the downstream backstop, but the design's own OQ-2 (and ORCH's already-filed ISS-0024 / #82) establishes that REQ-033 AC 4 is currently unstatable under a NO ACTION FK -- so the backstop is weaker than section 7.2 assumes. Recommend TEST-DESIGNER at Step 3 convert both into exit-code gates: assert pg_constraint.confdeltype = 'a' (NO ACTION) for instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey, and assert pg_indexes.indexdef for uq_active_definition contains the literal WHERE status = 'active' plus a behavioural check that a second :active row with the same name raises 23505. Per core-directives.md, an exit-code gate cannot be satisfied by renaming a label. Not a Step 1b check failure -- the design specifies both invariants concretely and section 4.5 already points at pg_indexes; this is a test-design strengthening, not a design gap.

Design section 3.1.2 and section 4.2 both cite connection.ex:1339 for 'an index does not inherit the table's prefix'; the line that actually renders quote_name(index.prefix, index.table) is 1335 (1339 is the interpolated column list). Five further immaterial drifts: migration.ex :name/:prefix/:unique are documented at :861-862/:863/:864 not :860-861/:862/:863; store.zig's NULLIF($6, '') binding is at :289 not :292; graph.ex's defstruct nodes: [], edges: [] is at :121 not :122-126; the design says a search across '146 migrations/*.sql' while R-Co currently has 151; enum.ex's bare-atom clause is :81-83 (:80 is the cond do). Separately, section 3.2.2 says a defaulted %Reference{} 'would emit an integer-typed column' -- connection.ex:1902's reference_column_type(:bigserial, _) actually emits bigint. In every case the substantive mechanism was independently confirmed real and the conclusion drawn from it is correct; recorded only so ELIXIR-DEV does not chase a wrong line and so the citations stay trustworthy as this design becomes a reference for REQ-030/REQ-033.

The design specifies two indexes beyond the three REQ-027's description enumerates ('Indexes: a unique index on (name, version), a partial unique index on name WHERE status = 'active', and a partial index on stage WHERE stage IS NOT NULL'): idx_def_status on process_definitions(status) (section 3.1.2, sourced to R-Co 004:39 and REQ-030's ?status= list filter at requirements.yaml:1319) and idx_snap_definition on instance_definition_snapshots(definition_id) (section 3.2.1, sourced to R-Co 004:68-69 and argued as load-bearing because Postgres does not auto-index the referencing side of an FK, so the NO ACTION check would sequentially scan). Both are R-Co-sourced, individually justified, and consistent with the design's own explicit 'deliberately NOT created' discipline (idx_def_name, idx_def_fts and the four 028_adp02 tenant-prefixed variants are declined with citations). Not a gate failure: no acceptance criterion states the index set is exhaustive, and both indexes are additive. Flagged so REVIEWER's Step 2d scope-creep check meets this on the record rather than first in the diff.

Two small hardening notes for downstream steps. (1) AC 5's parenthetical reads 'PD-01/PD-07/PD-08 sections'; section 7.1's ProcessDefinition moduledoc cites PD-01 and PD-07 but not PD-08, while section 7.2's snapshot moduledoc cites all three. The design's reading -- PD-01/PD-07 are the process_definitions sections, PD-08 the snapshot one -- is the sensible one and is argued explicitly in section 11's AC5 row, so this PASSES; but a hyper-literal later checker could read AC 5 as requiring all three tokens in both moduledocs. Recommend ELIXIR-DEV add a one-clause PD-08 cross-reference to ProcessDefinition's moduledoc (it is the table PD-08's snapshot references) so AC 5 holds under the most literal possible check at Step 5. (2) test/letflow/event_store/migrations_test.exs's section-4 guard test detects a broken guard correctly for the new migrations (assert at :499 is table-set-based and needs no edit), but its on_exit defensive cleanup at :470 only drops tables whose names appear in @event_store_tables -- so a guard failure on REQ-027's migrations would leave a stray public.process_definitions / public.instance_definition_snapshots behind in the test database after the failing run. Detection is unaffected; this is test hygiene for TEST-DESIGNER at Step 3.
